title: Preliminary HIPAA Breach Assessment — Data Theft Confirmed

fields.department: Office of the Chief Privacy Officer
fields.to: Information Security Officer (ISO), Administrator on Call (AOC), Public Information Officer (PIO)
fields.cc: General Counsel, Outside Cyber Counsel, FBI Cyber Division (via CISA)
fields.subject: Preliminary HIPAA Risk Assessment — Presumptive Breach Confirmed and Clock Started
fields.body:
Per 45 CFR 164.402, the encryption of protected health information in the CareLine EHR database constitutes a presumptive breach. The forensic evidence confirms that at least 40 patient records were exfiltrated and posted on a public leak site, including full face sheets with names, dates of birth, and medical record numbers.

The discovery time for the breach is formally established as 05:50 on Tuesday, March 3, 2026, based on the initial EHR unresponsiveness and the first confirmed alert from the managed detection service.

Given that the number of affected individuals exceeds 500 residents of Ohio, the requirements under 45 CFR 164.406 and 164.408 apply: a simultaneous notice to affected individuals, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the media must be issued within 60 calendar days of discovery.

No statement may be issued to the public that suggests the data was not accessed. All external communications must be cleared through the Office of the Chief Privacy Officer.

This assessment is preliminary. The full patient list will be compiled by the CPO’s team within the next 60 minutes.
fields.signatureBlock:
Joyce Tanaka
Chief Privacy Officer
Ottawa River Regional Medical Center

instructorNote: This memo confirms the breach and triggers the 60-day clock for HHS and media notifications. The AOC must now confirm the discovery time and ensure no public statement contradicts the CPO's position. The PIO is now under strict clearance control.
